item.title: A Traditional Christmas in the Castles of County Donegal
item.dc:creator: Sandra Thomas-Comenole
item.content:encoded:
In County Donegal, Ireland, Christmas unfolds amid the grandeur of a 19th-century castle, where festive dining, live music, and cherished traditions bring generations together. At Lough Eske Castle, the celebrations span four nights, from December 23 through 26, with seasonal meals, mulled wine and mince pies, and evenings of live entertainment. Christmas Day brings a festive buffet in the Castle Ballroom, while younger guests can look forward to a visit from Santa, a fairy trail, and activities designed especially for families. The celebrations begin well before Christmas itself, with a November lighting ceremony that welcomes the season and supports a local food drive organized with St. Vincent de Paul. From the castle’s historic interiors to the surrounding Donegal landscape, this Irish Christmas escape combines the atmosphere of a grand country estate with the warmth of local traditions and a spirit of community.

The Curated Take

A castle at Christmas evokes a sense of timeless celebration, but it is the traditions carried within its walls that make the experience meaningful. At Lough Eske, music, shared meals, and rituals for children sit alongside a commitment to supporting local families, connecting the pleasures of a festive escape with the generosity at the heart of the season. For travelers drawn to Ireland’s heritage and hospitality, Donegal offers a Christmas shaped as much by togetherness as by its historic setting.

item.title: A Caribbean Christmas of Beachside Celebrations in Antigua
item.dc:creator: Sandra Thomas-Comenole
item.content:encoded:
On Antigua’s southern coast, Christmas arrives with white-sand beaches, turquoise waters, and the warmth of Caribbean island life. At Carlisle Bay, the festive season runs from December 23 through January 3, bringing together holiday dining, wellness, sporting activities, and celebrations for all ages. Families can enjoy the Cool Kids Club’s seasonal program, with gingerbread decorating, beach bonfires and s’mores, a festive Christmas parade featuring Santa, and outdoor movies beneath the stars. Beyond the resort, island adventures range from swimming with rays at Stingray City to ziplining through the rainforest. As the year draws to a close, the celebrations take a glamorous turn with a Saturday Night Fever-themed New Year’s Eve, beginning with cocktails and live entertainment before a disco-inspired gala dinner, dancing, Champagne, and fireworks over the bay. A New Year’s Day steel-band barbecue continues the festivities, offering a sun-filled alternative to the traditional winter holiday.

The Curated Take

A festive escape in the Caribbean offers more than a change of climate. It creates space to experience familiar holiday rituals in a setting where the beach becomes the gathering place and celebrations stretch into warm evenings beside the sea. At Carlisle Bay, family adventures and playful seasonal traditions meet the glamour of a disco-inspired New Year’s Eve, making Antigua an appealing choice for travelers who want their holidays to feel both restorative and full of life. Here, the season is less about escaping Christmas than discovering a different way to celebrate it.

item.title: A Pura Vida Festive Season on Costa Rica’s Pacific Coast
item.dc:creator: Sandra Thomas-Comenole
item.content:encoded:
On Costa Rica’s Pacific coast, the festive season takes on a sunlit character, with oceanfront celebrations, cacao traditions, and evenings beneath the stars offering an alternative to winter’s familiar rituals. Beginning in November 2027, Waldorf Astoria Costa Rica Punta Cacique will welcome the holidays with experiences that bring together traditional seasonal pleasures and the country’s Pura Vida spirit. Guests can take part in festive mixology classes, gather for stargazing and s’mores, explore the art of chocolate-making, and experience traditional cacao ceremonies. As the year draws to a close, Wishes by the Sea offers an oceanfront New Year’s Eve celebration centered on reflection, fresh beginnings, and the possibilities of the year ahead. For travelers seeking a luxury festive escape in Costa Rica, the program offers a warm-weather alternative where local traditions, natural surroundings, and meaningful moments shape the holiday experience.

The Curated Take

A change of scenery can also be a change of rhythm. Along Costa Rica’s Pacific coast, festive traditions move outdoors, from evenings spent beneath a star-filled sky to cacao experiences rooted in the region’s cultural heritage. The emphasis on reflection and new beginnings brings a thoughtful dimension to a tropical holiday escape, inviting travelers to welcome the year ahead with a renewed sense of connection to nature, place, and the people around them.

item.title: An Enchanted Winter Forest in the Swiss Alps
item.dc:creator: Sandra Thomas-Comenole
item.content:encoded:
In Crans-Montana, Switzerland, the festive season unfolds among snow-covered Alpine peaks, where forest-inspired rituals, seasonal dining, and outdoor adventures create a distinctive winter escape. This holiday season, Six Senses Crans-Montana draws on the atmosphere of an enchanted winter forest, with experiences designed to connect guests with the natural world. Christmas Eve brings a five-course dinner at Wild Cabin, while Ora Bar & Lounge serves seasonal favorites. Wellness takes inspiration from the surrounding landscape through guided sound journeys and bespoke botanical fragrance creation, and the resort’s Earth Lab invites guests to craft natural ornaments, upcycled candles, and forest-inspired incense. Families can join festive baking, snow globe making, and wreath crafting through the Grow With Six Senses children’s program. As the year draws to a close, celebrations include a Winter Forest Gala Dinner at Les Cabanes and an eight-course Japanese menu at Byakko, alongside moonlit skiing, gourmet snowshoe experiences, and guided winter hikes through the Swiss Alps.

The Curated Take

Winter in the Alps offers more than snow-covered scenery; it creates an opportunity to experience the landscape through every sense. The scent of botanicals, the resonance of a guided sound journey, and the tactile pleasure of making something by hand bring a quieter dimension to the festive season. In Crans-Montana, these restorative rituals sit alongside alpine exploration and distinctive dining, offering a holiday experience that balances celebration with reconnection to nature.

item.title: Beyond the Plate: Chef Christian Alzaga on Slower Travel and Coastal Jungle Identity
item.dc:creator: Sandra Thomas-Comenole
item.content:encoded:
In an era where Tulum changes at breakneck speed, Chef Christian Alzaga—Executive Chef for Namron Hospitality and the culinary mind behind NÜ Tulum, which has been recommended in the MICHELIN Guide three years in a row—isn’t interested in dropping dish names or chasing hyper-fast dining trends. When we sat down to discuss the restaurant’s direction, Chef Alzaga offered a quiet counter-narrative: a call to slow down, respect the territory, and look past the hype. Below is the complete, unedited transcript of our conversation, paired with our curated town recommendations.

What is happening right now at NÜ Tulum? Are there any upcoming menu launches, new culinary concepts, or exciting updates we should explicitly highlight alongside this piece?

NÜ is currently in a phase of constant evolution. Rather than focusing solely on creating new dishes, we are working to deepen the narrative behind each dining experience. Our approach remains centered on building an emotional connection between our guests, the territory, and the ingredients we use.

At the moment, we are exploring new ways to integrate local products, contemporary techniques, and more immersive experiences that allow us to tell stories through cuisine, such as our tasting menu. Each season gives us the opportunity to reinterpret ingredients and continue shaping a proposal that reflects both the essence of Tulum and our culinary vision, as well as a part of who we are and what defines us.

For us, innovation is not simply about introducing something new; it is about finding more honest and thoughtful ways to express who we are as a restaurant and what we want to share with our guests.

[EDITORIAL FIELD NOTE: THE TASTING MENU]

Translating philosophy to the plate: NÜ’s multi-course tasting menus center around open-fire Mexican culinary techniques beneath the jungle canopy. Expect native ingredients like octopus, local recados (spice pastes), heirloom corn varieties, and wood-charred seasonal vegetables paired with artisanal mezcals.

What is your personal backstory with Tulum? What was the definitive moment, memory, or flavor profile that originally drew you to this coastal jungle?

My relationship with Tulum began long before I started working here. Like many people, I was initially drawn by its natural beauty, but what made me stay was the creative energy and cultural diversity that come together in this destination.

One of the things that impacted me most was discovering how simple ingredients can take on an entirely different identity when they are part of such a unique ecosystem. Understanding the connection between the sea, the jungle, the local communities, and the region’s producers helped me realize that cooking in Tulum goes far beyond following a recipe, it is a way of interpreting and expressing the territory itself.

As a chef, Tulum has taught me to observe more closely, listen more carefully, and create experiences where the surroundings play just as important a role as the dishes that arrive at the table.

“Cooking in Tulum goes far beyond following a recipe—it is a way of interpreting and expressing the territory itself.”

— Chef Christian Alzaga

If a true food lover only has time for one absolute must-visit spot in the area outside of your own kitchen, where are they going?

If I had to choose just one place, I would recommend stepping away from the usual route and exploring the smaller spaces where a deeper connection to the local community is still preserved. Some of the most memorable food experiences are often found not in large restaurants, but in a taquería, a family-run kitchen, or a local market where the ingredients speak for themselves.

I would also encourage visitors to spend time exploring Tulum town, visiting specialty coffee shops, discovering artisan bakeries, and experiencing culinary projects that work closely with regional producers. To truly understand Tulum’s food culture, it is important to experience both its contemporary gastronomic scene and the traditional culinary expressions that continue to shape the destination’s identity.

[CURATED GUIDE: TULUM PUEBLO]

Step away from the beach strip to explore three essential town-center culinary pillars: Mestixa for elevated Asian-Yucatecan dining, Italdo for artisan sourdough and Italian espresso in Veleta, and Taquería Honorio for iconic, slow-roasted cochinita pibil tacos served fresh on handmade tortillas.

Tulum has evolved incredibly fast. What is your #1 piece of insider advice for travelers visiting today to ensure they experience the most authentic version of the destination?

My number one piece of advice would be to slow down.

Many people arrive with a long list of places they want to visit, but Tulum’s true essence reveals itself when you take the time to observe and experience it at a more relaxed pace. Speaking with local producers, visiting nearby communities, learning about the region’s history, and understanding the relationship between nature and local culture can offer a much deeper and more authentic perspective.

Tulum remains an extraordinary destination for those seeking genuine experiences. Beyond the trends, its authenticity is found in its people, its ingredients, its stories, and the profound connection between the jungle, the sea, and those who have made this place their home.

Editor’s Note: NÜ Tulum is situated along the South Tulum Beach Road, nestled on the jungle side of the strip. While Executive Chef Christian Alzaga advocates for exploring the neighborhood’s humble family kitchens and town-center roasters by day, a table at NÜ by night remains one of the Riviera Maya’s most atmospheric candlelit dining experiences.

item.title: A Festive Alpine Escape at Carlton Hotel St. Moritz
item.dc:creator: Sandra Thomas-Comenole
item.content:encoded:
High above Lake St. Moritz, the snow-covered peaks of Switzerland’s Engadine Valley set the scene for a festive season defined by alpine elegance, exceptional dining, and winter adventure. At the five-star, all-suite Carlton Hotel St. Moritz, December brings a celebration of the season that pairs Michelin-starred gastronomy with the glamour of one of Switzerland’s most storied winter destinations. Highlights include a collaborative four-hands dinner with the Cerea Brothers of Da Vittorio and Swiss chef Andreas Caminada, the excitement of the FIS Ski World Cup on Corviglia, and two distinctive New Year’s Eve celebrations. Beyond the table, a dedicated Outdoor Butler can arrange bespoke ski tours, snow treks, horse-drawn carriage rides, husky sledding, and ice skating, while the designer boutiques of St. Moritz offer a different kind of winter indulgence.

The Curated Take

In St. Moritz, the festive season is as much about atmosphere as it is about celebration. From gliding through a snow-covered landscape by horse-drawn carriage to lingering over an exceptional alpine dinner, Carlton Hotel St. Moritz offers a way to experience the Swiss Alps that balances outdoor discovery with refined comfort. For travelers seeking a luxurious European Christmas or New Year’s escape, it is a setting where winter’s grandeur meets the enduring glamour of the Engadine.

item.title: Following the Silk Road to a Festive Season in the Maldives
item.dc:creator: Sandra Thomas-Comenole
item.content:encoded:
This festive season, the Maldives becomes a meeting point of cultures as Vakkaru Maldives draws inspiration from the historic Silk Road for nearly four weeks of celebrations, from December 13, 2026, through January 9, 2027. Set within the UNESCO Biosphere Reserve of Baa Atoll, the program brings together international cuisine, live entertainment, wellness experiences, and activities for families against the backdrop of the Indian Ocean. Highlights include a Christmas Eve gala dinner beneath the stars on Vakku Beach, sunset wine tastings on a private sandbank, and a Silk Road-inspired New Year’s Eve celebration featuring global flavors and fireworks over the water. At Merana Spa, Japanese holistic practitioner Yoko Kawaguchi leads a special residency, adding a restorative dimension to the festivities. The celebrations continue into January with Orthodox Christmas traditions, extending the holiday season beyond the usual calendar and inviting guests to experience the Maldives through a distinctly international lens.

The Curated Take

The historic Silk Road was more than a route for trade; it was a passage through which ideas, traditions, and cultures met and evolved. Bringing that spirit to a Maldivian island creates an intriguing approach to the festive season, where culinary discovery and cultural influences become part of the celebration. For travelers seeking a luxury holiday escape with a sense of connection beyond the shoreline, Vakkaru’s program offers a reminder that some of the most rewarding journeys happen when different traditions share the same table.

item.title: A Classic New York Christmas, from Holiday Carols to the Times Square Ball Drop
item.dc:creator: Sandra Thomas-Comenole
item.content:encoded:
New York City takes on a special kind of magic during the holidays, when festive music, seasonal treats, and beloved traditions transform Midtown into a winter wonderland. At InterContinental New York Barclay, the season brings classic New York celebrations together with thoughtful experiences for families and travelers of all ages. Thanksgiving and Christmas dining at The Parlour sets the scene for seasonal gatherings, while the annual Barclay Express: Cookies & Cocoa invites families to decorate cookies and sip hot chocolate. Throughout the week of December 14, holiday choirs fill the lobby with music, and a postcard station offers guests the chance to send greetings to loved ones or Santa, whose replies may arrive at their guestrooms by way of the hotel’s elves. Younger guests can retreat to the Petit Chalet, a cozy A-frame hideaway stocked with blankets, pillows, and classic board games. The celebrations culminate on New Year’s Eve, when guests can welcome the year ahead at The Parlour while watching the iconic Times Square Ball Drop.

The Curated Take

Few cities make the holidays feel as cinematic as New York, where familiar rituals take on an extra sparkle against the energy of Midtown. From handwritten holiday greetings and carols in the lobby to watching the Times Square Ball Drop without stepping into the winter crowds, the Barclay’s seasonal experiences offer a more intimate way to enjoy the city’s festive spirit. For families and couples planning a New York holiday escape, it is an invitation to experience the season through small traditions, shared moments, and the unmistakable atmosphere of the city at its most celebratory.

item.title: A Season of Holiday Traditions in Plymouth, Michigan
item.dc:creator: Sandra Thomas-Comenole
item.content:encoded:
From Thanksgiving gatherings to Christmas magic and New Year’s Eve celebrations, Plymouth, Michigan, offers a festive-season escape filled with family traditions and elegant occasions. At Saint John’s Resort, the holidays begin with a Thanksgiving feast featuring traditional favorites and interactive dessert stations, followed the next day by a Christmas tree lighting in the Monarch Courtyard, where twinkling lights, live carolers, hot cocoa, and fireside gatherings welcome the season. Families can add a little enchantment to their December stay with a holiday sleepover experience that includes an in-room visit from one of Santa’s helpers, a bedtime story, breakfast, and a special meeting with Santa. As the year draws to a close, The Wine Grotto hosts a New Year’s Eve celebration with an elaborate buffet, live music, and an evening designed for welcoming 2027. Together, these seasonal experiences make the resort an appealing destination for a festive family getaway or a celebratory holiday stay in the Detroit area.

The Curated Take

The holidays often become most memorable through the rituals shared along the way, from the first lights on a Christmas tree to the excitement of a child awaiting a visit from Santa. In Plymouth, Saint John’s Resort brings these moments together with celebrations for different generations, balancing family-friendly traditions with sophisticated dining and a spirited New Year’s gathering. For travelers seeking a holiday escape closer to home, it offers an opportunity to turn familiar seasonal customs into a special occasion without an elaborate journey.

item.title: Winter Wildlife Encounters in Jackson Hole, Wyoming
item.dc:creator: Sandra Thomas-Comenole
item.content:encoded:
Winter transforms Jackson Hole, Wyoming, into a remarkable setting for wildlife watching, as snow-covered landscapes make animal coats and tracks stand out against the white terrain. Sunrise and sunset safaris with local naturalist guides offer opportunities to observe elk, moose, bighorn sheep, and other wildlife while taking in views of the Teton Range. Snowshoeing excursions provide a closer connection to the region’s ecology, while dog sledding brings a more exhilarating way to explore the valley. At the National Elk Refuge, seasonal sleigh rides offer a memorable perspective on one of the area’s defining wildlife spectacles, as thousands of elk gather across protected winter habitat. For travelers planning a winter nature escape, Jackson Hole combines extraordinary wildlife encounters with access to Grand Teton National Park and the surrounding mountain landscape, while the Wyoming Inn offers a convenient base for exploring the region’s outdoor attractions.

The Curated Take

There is something extraordinary about encountering wildlife on its own terms, with a vast winter landscape creating the conditions to observe rather than simply pass through. In Jackson Hole, tracks etched into fresh snow and herds gathered across the National Elk Refuge reveal a different dimension of the American West. Guided by local experts who interpret the connections between animals and their environment, these experiences offer more than a sighting: they invite travelers to understand the rhythms of a wild landscape in winter.
